extracted.intended_audience: mathematics instructors/teachers (college or secondary) using PAR packets and peer-assisted reflection to improve teaching and student work
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and using PAR (Peer-Assisted Reflection) packets for math problem-solving and proof tasks to structure student draft → feedback → revision cycles and instructor/peer observation. Includes practical actions instructors can take to build supportive communities and run PAR activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take a concrete step to build community
rubrics_metrics.description: Think back to the guiding question of the chapter: What is a concrete step you plan to take to be in community with your colleagues and work together to improve your teaching?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt for instructors to identify a specific, actionable step to collaborate with colleagues around teaching improvement; intended to be used in conjunction with others who will have different responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and reflect on your teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Record yourself teaching and watch the video. What do you notice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use video self-observation as a reflective tool to notice behaviors, interactions, and teaching moves that may not be obvious in the moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange a peer observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a colleague in your network who can perform a peer observation for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a colleague who can give formative, supportive observations; follow up with discussion and use observations to inform practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate informal collegial exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite a colleague out for coffee to share with them some ideas you have learned from this book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use low-stakes meetings to disseminate ideas, build relationships, and seed collaborative change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a sympathetic administrator who might be willing to support your efforts. Have a meeting with them to share the work you’re doing and your vision for transforming teaching. Can you get their support?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage administrators to gain resources, legitimacy, or policy-level backing for instructional change initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run a faculty/staff book club
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a group of colleagues to run a book club with. Run the club!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize collective reading and discussion to spread practices and sustain momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form an EQUIP Learning Community
rubrics_metrics.description: Form an EQUIP Learning Community with your peers. If you need help getting started, contact the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an ongoing structured community for implementation and mutual support (contact info provided for help getting started).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on prior collaborative learning experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about the last time you learned something in community with others? What was it, and how did that experience go?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal reflection on past collaborative learning to inform design of future community learning activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAR Process stages
rubrics_metrics.description: PAR Process: Draft → Reflect → Exchange Feedback → Revise → Submit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These stages structure student work: drafting at home, reflection at home, exchanging feedback during class, revising at home, and submitting in class; explicitly map where each stage occurs (e.g., 'Tuesday Class', 'Wednesday Class').

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem task specification (Filling Bottles)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are filling up bottles with liquid coming from a tap at a constant rate. 1. For each bottle, sketch a graph of the height of liquid in the bottle as a function of time. 2. For each bottle, sketch a graph of the rate of change of the height of liquid as a function of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly-stated task expectations (what students must produce); used to anchor peer feedback and revision. The task defines observable work products for PAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student reflection using icons
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn the page and check off the icons for things you think you did well; circle the icons for things you would like feedback on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured self-assessment: students mark strengths and areas for feedback before peer exchange to focus feedback and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback structure header: Feedback Provided By / Suggestions / Communication / Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback sections to be completed by peers: 'Feedback Provided By:' followed by areas for 'Suggestions', 'Communication', and 'Strengths'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure peer feedback identifies both strengths and suggestions and comments on communication; prompts peers to be specific and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show all steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Show All Steps
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer feedback should note whether the student has shown all steps of reasoning or computation; missing steps are a common target for suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain why, not just what
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain Why, Not Just What
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback should encourage students to provide explanations of reasoning and justification rather than only stating results or steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pronouns / be precise
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid Pronouns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage clear mathematical writing by avoiding ambiguous pronouns; prefer explicit references to variables, functions, or objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Correct Definitions (e.g., (x, y))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and feedback should check that students invoke and use precise, correct definitions where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define variables and units
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Variables, Units, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should explicitly define any variables and their units; peers should flag omissions or ambiguities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Create Diagrams
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage inclusion of appropriate diagrams/representations; peers should note where diagrams would aid understanding or where existing diagrams are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (Correct setup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct Setup
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer feedback should evaluate whether the problem was set up correctly (equations, assumptions); incorrect setups should be identified with suggestions to fix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate Calculations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check arithmetic/ algebraic manipulations for correctness; peers should point out calculation errors and their effects on conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve multiple ways
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve Multiple Ways
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and value multiple solution approaches; peers can suggest alternative methods or note when multiple approaches clarify understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer Reasonable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the final answer is reasonable in context (units, magnitude, limiting behavior); peers should flag implausible results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other feedback (open)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other (Write Below)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space for peers to give miscellaneous comments not covered by predefined categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback should list strengths explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengths
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer feedback should include an explicit list of strengths to balance suggestions and reinforce good practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation protocol for proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Write your solution in the left column. The right column is used for annotations. If you provide feedback to your peer, you will annotate their solution. After class, you will annotate your own solution as well (and write 'self' on the annotated by line). In your submission, use the annotation column to explain how you did (or didn’t) respond to peer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two-column layout: left = solution; right = annotations for feedback and later self-reflection. Require marking 'annotated by' (peer or self) to document feedback provenance and require students to record their response to peer feedback in final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem specification for proof PAR packet
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem Statement: Continuity is a point-wise property of functions. In class, we also defined uniform continuity as a property across the entire domain of the function. 1. In your own words, describe the difference between continuity and uniform continuity. 2. Consider the function f(x) = x^2. On what domains is it continuous? Prove your conjectures using the definition of continuity and its negation. 3. Again consider f(x) = x^2. On what domains is it uniformly continuous? Prove your conjectures using the definition of uniform continuity and its negation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear assignment specifying conceptual explanation and formal proofs using definitions (and negations) — sets expectations for depth, rigor, and use of precise definitions in peer feedback and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft vs Submission artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish DRAFT vs SUBMISSION stages (pages labeled 'Draft (Page 1/2)' and 'Submission (Page 1/2)')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate artifacts for drafts (used for reflection and feedback) and final submissions (which should include evidence of revision and responses to feedback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate your own solution after peer feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: After class, annotate your own solution as well (and write 'self' on the annotated by line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require metacognitive follow-up where students annotate how they revised (or why they didn't) in response to peer comments; helps instructors assess engagement with feedback.
